text:
Mika Zibanejad passed 1,000 NHL games last season and keeps climbing the Rangers' record books; Newsday wrote this month that he's turning into one of the franchise's all-time greats. At 33 he has 20 points in 23 games, six goals on 5.6 expected, which is about exactly what his chances deserve.

The concern is the other end of the ice. At five on five the Rangers get only 44% of the shot attempts with him on, and they're a little worse with him than without. His line with Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault wins the quality battle (55% of the expected goals) while losing the volume one, which is a fine line to walk.

The shot is still elite: NHL Edge puts his hardest at the 97th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming on the power play, and that's still where he does his best work.

What to watch: he scored the Rangers' first goal against Carolina on a tip, his ninth point in ten games. The production is fine. Whether the line can tilt the ice is the question.
